{{< include _setup.qmd >}}

`rieszreg` holds the shared abstractions; pick at least one implementation package for an actual learner.

## Python

All six packages live in one GitHub repo, [rieszreg/rieszreg](https://github.com/rieszreg/rieszreg), under `packages/`:

| Package | Learner |
|---|---|
| `rieszreg` | shared estimands, losses, and sklearn glue |
| `rieszboost` | gradient boosting |
| `krrr` | kernel ridge regression |
| `forestriesz` | random forests |
| `riesztree` | a single decision tree |
| `riesznet` | neural networks |

The repo is a [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) workspace. One command installs every package into `.venv/` at the repo root:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/rieszreg/rieszreg.git
cd rieszreg
uv sync --all-packages --all-extras --all-groups
```

`--all-groups` adds the `docs` dependency group (`causaldata`, `matplotlib`, and a few others). The real-data examples need it: `packages/rieszboost/examples/lalonde_ate.py`, `packages/rieszboost/examples/nhefs_shift.py`, and the [custom estimation](estimation/custom.qmd) page load their data from `causaldata`. Leave the flag off if you only need the learners.

`rieszboost`'s `XGBoostBackend` requires OpenMP. On macOS:

```sh
brew install libomp
```

Linux distributions (and GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest) ship `libgomp1`; no extra step is needed. `krrr` has no system prerequisites. `forestriesz` depends on `econml`, which ships prebuilt wheels for macOS arm64+x86_64 and ubuntu — no compiler required. `riesztree` (which `forestriesz` also uses) builds a small Cython extension during install, so it needs a C compiler (Xcode command-line tools on macOS, `gcc` on Linux). `riesznet` depends on `torch>=2.0`; CPU wheels are fetched automatically, GPU wheels need a `--index-url` per the PyTorch install matrix.

### Combining `rieszboost` and `riesznet` in one process

The macOS pip wheels for `xgboost` and `torch` each bundle their own `libomp.dylib`. When both are loaded into one Python process, the two OpenMP runtimes can deadlock during a fit ([troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd)). Two install paths avoid this:

- **conda-forge** — installs `xgboost` and `pytorch` against a single shared `llvm-openmp`, so the conflict cannot occur:
  ```sh
  conda install -c conda-forge xgboost pytorch
  pip install -e packages/rieszreg/python packages/rieszboost/python packages/riesznet/python
  ```
- **thread-limit env vars** — keep the uv install above and set `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` (and `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`) in the shell or at the top of every script that uses both backends. See the [troubleshooting page](troubleshooting.qmd) for the full discussion and options including `threadpoolctl.threadpool_limits` for finer-grained control.

### Verify

The chunks below import each package and exercise its public entry point. Failure to import or instantiate raises immediately.

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

## Python

```{python}
import importlib.metadata as _md
import rieszreg, rieszboost, krrr, forestriesz, riesztree, riesznet
from rieszreg import ATE
from rieszboost import RieszBooster
from krrr import KernelRieszRegressor
from forestriesz import AugForestRieszRegressor, ForestRieszRegressor
from riesztree import RieszTreeRegressor
from riesznet import RieszNet

# Construct one estimator from each backend to confirm wiring.
estimand = ATE()
RieszBooster(estimand=estimand, n_estimators=5)
KernelRieszRegressor(estimand=estimand, lambda_grid=(1e-2,))
AugForestRieszRegressor(estimand=estimand, n_estimators=10)
ForestRieszRegressor(estimand=estimand, n_estimators=10)
RieszTreeRegressor(estimand=estimand)
RieszNet(estimand=estimand, hidden_sizes=(8,), epochs=1)

for pkg in ("rieszreg", "rieszboost", "krrr", "forestriesz", "riesztree", "riesznet"):
    print(f"{pkg:<12} {_md.version(pkg)}")
```

## R

```{r}
# `_setup.qmd` already dev-loaded rieszreg + rieszboost. Reference the
# exported symbols and instantiate one R6 wrapper to confirm reticulate
# is wired through to the Python venv.
stopifnot(is.function(ATE), R6::is.R6Class(RieszBooster))
booster <- RieszBooster$new(estimand = ATE(), n_estimators = 5L)
cat("rieszreg + rieszboost R wrappers OK (",
    class(booster)[1], ")\n", sep = "")
```

:::

## R wrappers (optional)

The R packages are R6 wrappers that call the Python implementations through [reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/). They do not require any separate algorithmic dependency.

First-time setup:

1. Install the R package dependencies:
   ```r
   install.packages(c(
     "reticulate", "R6",          # required: Python bridge + R6 classes
     "pkgload",                   # required for `pkgload::load_all` below
     "rsample", "xgboost"         # optional: used in the landing-page R quickstart
                                  # and the estimation/custom-code page
   ))
   ```
2. Install the six R packages from the repo root:
   ```sh
   Rscript tools/r/install.R              # all six
   Rscript tools/r/install.R rieszboost   # rieszreg + one learner package
   ```
   Then `library(rieszreg); library(rieszboost)` in R. To dev-load from the source tree instead, run from the repo root and load `rieszreg` first, since every learner package imports from it:
   ```r
   pkgload::load_all("packages/rieszreg/r/rieszreg")
   pkgload::load_all("packages/rieszboost/r/rieszboost")
   pkgload::load_all("packages/krrr/r/krrr")
   pkgload::load_all("packages/forestriesz/r/forestriesz")
   pkgload::load_all("packages/riesztree/r/riesztree")
   pkgload::load_all("packages/riesznet/r/riesznet")
   ```
   Load `rieszboost` and `riesznet` in separate R sessions on macOS (see [Combining `rieszboost` and `riesznet` in one process](#combining-rieszboost-and-riesznet-in-one-process)).
3. Point reticulate at the uv venv before loading any package. Set the environment variable before R starts:
   ```sh
   export RETICULATE_PYTHON=/path/to/rieszreg/.venv/bin/python
   ```
   Or call `use_python_rieszboost(".venv/bin/python")` (each package has its own `use_python_<pkg>()`).

The R API exposes every built-in estimand, every loss, and the full estimator interface for each backend. The symbolic tracer for custom `m()` is Python-only; see [r-interface](r-interface.qmd) for how to call it from R.

## Tests

Run each Python test suite separately from the repo root:

```{.bash}
for pkg in rieszreg rieszboost krrr forestriesz riesztree riesznet; do
  uv run pytest "packages/$pkg/python/tests" -q
done
```

The R tests use the R packages installed in step 2 above. Run `riesznet` in its own R session:

```{.bash}
export RETICULATE_PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python
Rscript -e '
  library(rieszreg)
  for (pkg in c("rieszboost", "krrr", "forestriesz", "riesztree")) {
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
    testthat::test_dir(file.path("packages", pkg, "r", pkg, "tests", "testthat"))
  }
'
Rscript -e '
  library(rieszreg); library(riesznet)
  testthat::test_dir("packages/riesznet/r/riesznet/tests/testthat")
'
```
